Design decisions before writing:
- `Iterable<K>` and `keySet()` both go on the interface so the `HashMapOperations`-typed variable in the demo can use them without casting
- `keySet()` returns `Set<K>` (snapshot, not a live view — consistent with the simplicity of this implementation)
- `KeyIterator` is a non-static inner class — it needs direct access to `table`, `capacity`, and `DELETED` from the enclosing instance; contrast with `HashNode`, which is `static` because it holds no outer reference
- The iterator scans the flat table array linearly, skipping `null` and `DELETED` slots

content.text:
All four strategy runs confirm the iterator and `keySet()` each return exactly 20 live keys after 20 inserts, and the small-map demo shows both features working correctly. Summary of every change:

**`HashMapOperations.java`**
- Added `import java.util.Set`
- Extends `Iterable<K>` — the `iterator()` method is inherited from the interface, so all implementors are forced to provide it
- Added `Set<K> keySet()` to the contract

**`HashMap.java`**
- Added four imports: `HashSet`, `Iterator`, `NoSuchElementException`, `Set`
- `iterator()` — delegates to the new `KeyIterator`; `@Override` satisfies `Iterable<K>` via the interface
- `keySet()` — linear scan of the flat `table` array, collecting non-null, non-DELETED keys into a `HashSet` snapshot
- `KeyIterator` — private **non-static** inner class (needs `table`, `capacity`, and `DELETED` from the enclosing instance, unlike `HashNode` which is `static`); `advance()` is called in the constructor and after each `next()` so `index` always points at the next live slot or past-the-end; throws `NoSuchElementException` on over-iteration per the `Iterator` contract

**`open_addressing_linear_probing.java`**
- `runDemo` now counts keys via the iterator and checks `keySet().size()` against the expected 20 for each strategy
- A dedicated "Iterator & keySet" section at the end of `main` uses a three-entry map to make the actual key output readable
